## Mechanism
The tracked link is substitution in the ration, carried in both directions: cheap feed wheat displaces corn and softens corn demand, and higher corn prices pull feed-wheat demand and lift the wheat-corn spread floor, supporting Chicago wheat. That is the whole feed-side channel the model gives — it is a demand reallocation between two grains, not a supply effect on either.

On corn, the loud readings lean both ways. Price-supportive: the stocks-to-use ratio at 12.14% of domestic use for 2026/27 [N73], past the desk's tight line and at the 16th percentile of its own record [N75], and weekly export shipments of 1900 thousand MT in the week to 17 September 2026 [N58], ahead of pace at the 85th percentile [N60]. Those two are the amplifying pair the model names — fast exports against a tight buffer accelerate a squeeze — though only two of the three conditions that pattern asks for are showing, so it is not in force. Leaning the other way: harvested area at 35.82 M ha, the 98th percentile of its own record [N55][N57], which loosens supply; and the warm-phase tropical Pacific anomaly at +1.8 degC in July 2026, the 93rd percentile of its own record [N19][N21], declared to move corn in the opposite direction at medium confidence, rising in each of the last eight months. I lean to the tight buffer dominating into the nearby: the stocks-to-use edge is high confidence and already realised in the sheet, while the Pacific warm-phase edge is medium confidence and acts through a yield that is not yet priced.

On wheat, the same warm phase is declared price-pressuring [N22], and the export leg is weak — 43.1 thousand MT shipped in the week to 17 September 2026 [N80], behind pace at the 38th percentile [N82]. The counterweight is acreage: US all-classes harvested area at 12.97 M ha, the 1st percentile of its own record [N16][N18], falling in each of the last two marketing years, declared to move wheat in the opposite direction at high confidence with a one-to-three-quarter lag — so that area collapse is the price-supportive leg on wheat, with its effect window running to around September 2027. Reading the pair on the feed axis: corn's tightness is what would bid feed wheat, and wheat's own sheet is too loose to squeeze on its own.

## Cross-commodity
Two commodities' own-marketing-year stocks-to-use, each measured on its own balance sheet as ending stocks over domestic use, world-comparable as a dimensionless fraction:
- CBOT corn, United States 2026/27: 12.14% of domestic use [N13]
- Wheat, all classes, United States 2026/27: 65.22% of domestic use [N14]

Corn's buffer is razor-thin and wheat's is far larger. That asymmetry is where the convexity sits: with a buffer that thin, a corn supply or demand shock has little cushion to absorb it and the price response is convex and right-tailed, while an equally sized wheat shock lands into a deep cushion and the response is closer to linear. It also caps the feed-substitution channel's power — the wheat pool has volume to lend the ration, so the substitution bleeds corn demand off before corn can run far, which flattens the right tail rather than removing it. Corn's fundamentals point to firmer prices, wheat's own sheet to softer ones, with the feed bid as wheat's offset.

- Wheat 2026/27 projections, same date: production 1,531 Million Bushels [N6], total domestic use 1,099 [N8], exports 775 [N9], ending stocks 717 [N7], projected farm price 6.4 $/bu [N10]. All of those are the USDA's own projections for a marketing year the record has not closed, not settled figures.
- The feed channel itself, 2026/27: corn feed use 151,137 thousand MT [N11] against all-classes wheat feed use 2,177 thousand MT [N12] — different commodities, so read each on its own sheet.
- Price tape, December 2026 delivery: corn 527.5 US cents/bushel, up 88 over sixty-three sessions and at the 94th percentile of the window fetched [N89][N93][N94]; Chicago wheat 707 US cents/bushel, up 83 over sixty-three sessions, 92nd percentile [N95][N99][N100]; MATIF December 2026 milling wheat 236.75 EUR/t, at the 29th percentile of its own fetched window [N101][N105] — a euro-priced board that is never ranked against the two dollar boards. The corn-minus-wheat spread asked for reads -179.5 US cents/bushel on 24 September 2026 [N15]; a governed spread series is not otherwise served, so the gap is characterised in words only.
- A settled US corn season-average farm price pair the record carries: $3.56/bu in MY2019/20 [N116] rising to $4.53/bu in MY2020/21 [N117] — survey-based USDA season-average actuals, not futures settles and not a forecast.

Those are dated 2011 to 2024 and describe past marketing years, not today's ration. The chain the page carries into corn runs from the blended fertilizer price through US wheat harvested area, then ending stocks, then the calendar spread. Link one: blended fertilizer peaked at the 79th percentile in April 2026 [N79] and now reads the 63rd [N78], through 10 September 2026; the model expects it to move harvested area in the opposite direction, and the readings run against that. Links three and four — ending stocks to the calendar spread, and the spread to corn — carry no series at all, so the chain stops being quantified there and I will not bridge it. The only dated report at the ending-stocks link is 11 April 2024, outside the lag the model allows for it [E10], and the record holds no past occasion of area sitting this far out with an ending-stocks reading to measure. ## Mechanism
Stocks are the buffer that decides whether a supply shock is convex or absorbed. For palm, month-end Malaysian inventory is the model's highest-confidence pressure channel: rising stocks loosen the balance and press the price, at zero to one quarter. Working against that, drought in the palm belt cuts fresh fruit bunch formation with a two-to-four-quarter biological lag — the longest lag in this complex, which is why a dry reading today is a 2027 supply story, not a 2026 one. On rapeseed, the model's substitution edge runs palm -> rapeseed oil with a positive sign: palm sets the floor of the vegetable-oil complex, so a palm squeeze lifts rapeseed oil rather than competing with it. These two are one pair, not two trades.

## The record
- Chinese stocks, January to June 2026: palm +14,900 MT (+2.1 %) [N12]; rapeseed oil +170,000 MT (+70.25 %) [N13], reaching 412,000 MT in June 2026 [N11] against palm's 724,100 MT [N10].
- Malaysia: closing stocks 2.82 MMT, August 2026 [N98], 94th percentile of their own record [N99], past the desk's high line, rising in each of the last five months [N138], with 2.18 months of export cover [N9].
- Palm belt dryness: longest dry-day run at 1.25 z for August 2026 [N14], +2.7 sigma on its trailing ten years [N15], 97th percentile [N16], rising three months running — past the line the desk calls severe.
- Europe: rapeseed stocks-to-use at 9.42 % of domestic use for 2026/27 [N62], 77th percentile [N64], past the line called ample, though falling over the last marketing year; crush at 25.4 MMT [N50]; Ukraine 4.35 MMT [N53], Canada 22.5 MMT [N56], Australia 7.8 MMT [N59] all near the top of their own records. Four of the seven conditions of the price-pressuring glut-with-demand-loss pattern are showing on Chicago-quoted terms — the pattern is in force on the count the model asks for.

- Dated documents are thin and old for this pair: the newest behind this answer is 13 March 2023, noting rapeseed and soybean oil filling the sunflower gap in China [E2]; an older read from 2013 has weaker soyoil and rapeoil adding to softer palm sentiment [E3].

## The chain
Working from Brent to palm: the Brent price against its own five-year record sits at 0.51 z for August 2026 [N100], the 68th percentile [N102], after peaking at the 98th in April 2026 [N103]. The model expects crude to push fertilizer costs the same way; no series is served at that link. Fertilizer is expected to push European harvested area the other way, and European area is at the 70th percentile and rising since 2024 — that link runs against the direction the model expects. European stocks-to-use then sits at 9.42 % [N62], falling since 2025, and the model expects it to move palm the opposite way; there the readings agree. The record holds no past occasion with Brent this far out and a fertilizer reading to measure, and the front price does not reach back that far. The one dated document at this chain, from 15 March 2022 on rapeseed oil strengthening as biodiesel feedstock while palm stays high [E11], falls outside the lag the model allows. A second chain runs from Brent to Chicago soybean oil, through rubber-area substitution — no series there — and into Malaysian stocks [N98]; it settles no direction. One hundred chains run into these four markets in all. Where the pair is set against each other, the record leans to palm carrying the directional information: its stocks reading is high-confidence, quantified and moving, while the rapeseed leg's ENSO edge is low-confidence.

## Spillovers
El Niño reads +1.8 degC for July 2026 [N17], +2.4 sigma [N18], 93rd percentile [N19], rising eight months running. It is one reading declared on thirty-four other markets — twenty-eight in the same direction, six opposite. Its signs differ by market and must be kept apart: on palm the model declares it in the same direction at two-to-four quarters, high confidence; on MATIF rapeseed, ICE canola and ZCE rapeseed oil it is declared in the opposite direction at one-to-three quarters, low confidence. The warm phase is what is in force; the cool-phase entries on those same series are what would apply in the other phase, not a second reading. That asymmetry is the heart of your question: the same ocean state is price-supportive for palm and, on a weaker edge, price-pressuring for the rapeseed complex. ICE canola settled 824.6 CAD/t on 2026-09-23 [N119], the 96th percentile of the window read [N124]; ZCE rapeseed oil settled 10236 CNY/t on 2026-09-24 [N125].

That is a timing fork, not a contradiction: near-term loose, later-dated right tail. Convexity sits where they cross — a buffer above two months of export cover [N9] absorbs the first tranche of yield loss linearly; once it draws down into a confirmed dry-driven output cut, the response turns convex, and the substitution edge drags rapeseed oil up with it.

## Mechanism
Palm reaches soyoil through the substitution gate: a wide soyoil premium over palm pushes price-sensitive buyers into palm; a palm supply shock pushes them back onto soyoil. That gate is priced, not asserted — palm at 1,117 USD/mt and soyoil at 1,638 USD/mt, both August 2026 [N11][N13], with soyoil the further above its own five-year mean at 1.21 sigma versus palm's 0.27 sigma [N14][N12]. Palm sits at the deep discount, so incremental food demand rations toward palm; that is what caps soyoil's food leg even as its fuel leg tightens.

Two palm-side forces run against each other. Rising Malaysian stocks [N100] loosen prompt supply now. The severe dry-spell run in the palm belt [N24] works through frond and inflorescence development into fresh fruit bunch yields with the model's two-to-four quarter lag, so it is a forward tightening, not a present one — conditional on that lag, its window opens around November 2026 and closes around August 2027. Against both, Russian sunflower oil production at 7.81 MMT for 2026/27, the 99th percentile of its own record [N30][N32], is declared to move palm the opposite way: a large competing soft oil slows palm offtake and builds stocks.

## The record
The asked comparison, August 2026: palm minus soyoil at -521 USD/mt [N23]. A same-date October 2026 spread was not computed — palm settles in USD/metric ton and soyoil in US cents/lb, and no conversion is made here.

These are different countries on different sheets — not a like-for-like tightness ranking — but the direction is clear: soyoil's sheet is the constrained one. World-basis stocks-to-use for palm and for soyoil carry no figure at this as-of; the record is silent there and I assert nothing for it.
